name: Rust
description: The language for all code in the repo unless an exception says otherwise.
claude: Official rust-analyzer-lsp Claude Code plugin.

name: Dioxus
description: The framework for web, desktop and mobile apps. New work uses 0.7; blueeel and sparkhill/webapp are still on 0.6, and cahokia's version is pinned on purpose (AGENTS.md).

name: dioxus-ssr
description: Render Dioxus components in plain Rust tests to check text, links and classes without a browser.

name: pulldown-cmark
description: CommonMark Markdown to HTML in Rust, compiled to wasm; pane renders plans, decisions and retros with it, raw HTML shown as text.

name: Bevy
description: The game engine.

name: Axum
description: The HTTP server framework. Its only user, luggage, is on hold.

name: utoipa
description: OpenAPI documents generated from Axum handlers (spelled "Utopia" in the standards README).

name: Clap
description: Argument parsing for traditional CLIs.

name: Ratatui
description: The framework for terminal UIs. No project uses it yet.

name: Tokio
description: The async runtime for IO-bound work.

name: Rayon
description: Data parallelism for compute-bound work. No project uses it yet.

name: tracing
description: The only logging library.

name: anyhow
description: Error handling in applications.

name: thiserror
description: Error types in libraries.

name: nalgebra
description: Linear algebra. No project uses it yet.

name: ndarray
description: N-dimensional arrays and matrices. No project uses it yet.

name: Pingora
description: The reverse proxy framework. No project uses it yet.

name: inkwell (LLVM)
description: LLVM bindings for the my_lang compiler. Needs LLVM headers, so it can't build in cloud sandboxes. Use only for compiler work.

name: TypeScript and Node.js
description: Allowed only for VS Code extensions and the Playwright e2e specs. Jim dislikes the Node dependency; decision 0005 (proposed) keeps it limited to e2e tests.
claude: Official typescript-lsp Claude Code plugin.

name: Perseus and Sycamore 0.8
description: Don't start new sites on them; use Dioxus. The existing sites stay pinned to sycamore 0.8 because perseus 0.4.2 needs it.

name: mise
description: The task runner and tool installer for every project: the same ci, fix, build, test, dev, release and deploy tasks everywhere, from shared files in standards/tasks.

name: lefthook
description: Git hooks that run the audit and each affected project's CI before every commit and push. Making them work in cloud sandboxes is an open TODO.

name: gitleaks
description: Secret scanning (SEC-001): the staged diff in pre-commit, the pushed commits in pre-push, the PR's commits in PR CI and the whole history weekly. Pinned in standards/scripts/secrets-check.sh; our rules in .gitleaks.toml.

name: cargo-deny
description: RustSec advisories and crate sources for every Cargo.lock (SEC-003), as warnings: in the hooks and PR CI where a lockfile changed, and nightly over all of them. Pinned in standards/scripts/deps-check.sh; config in standards/deny.toml. Licence checks come later.

name: zizmor
description: GitHub Actions workflow audit (SEC-005), as warnings: in the hooks and PR CI (Workflow audit) where a workflow changed, and nightly over all of them. Offline. Pinned in standards/scripts/workflows-check.sh; ignores in .github/zizmor.yml.

name: cargo-llvm-cov
description: Line coverage of every Rust project each night (COV-001, a warning under 80% for now), stored on the coverage-results branch with the README badge (Jim, 2026-11-27). Pinned in standards/scripts/coverage.sh.

name: Playwright
description: Browser end-to-end tests, and the recorded smoke UAT (screenshots, video, trace) that decision 0001 makes the default evidence on PRs.
claude: Playwright MCP server (Microsoft).

name: Playwright on a system browser
description: Proposed in decision 0005: launch Chromium tests on the machine's own Chrome instead of Playwright's download, so they run in sandboxes. Rust WebDriver (fantoccini, thirtyfour), CDP (chromiumoxide) and WebDriver BiDi clients were compared and not recommended yet.
claude: Playwright MCP server (Microsoft).

name: Marp
description: Slide decks written in Markdown, used for the weekly deep project reviews.

name: Kokoro text-to-speech
description: Open-weight voice (kokoro-onnx, Apache 2.0) that narrates the review deck demo videos, run locally with ffmpeg and Playwright's video recording. Brings Python in for that one script only. Decision 0025 (proposed).

name: cross
description: Always use it for cross compilation. No project uses it yet.

name: wasm-bindgen
description: Builds the web (WebAssembly) version of Bevy games for Cloudflare Pages, through the bevy-game release:web task. The CLI version must match wasm-bindgen in the game's Cargo.lock.

name: cargo-apk
description: Packages Bevy games as Android APKs for playtesting (release:android). Unmaintained upstream but still what Bevy 0.14's NativeActivity build supports; cross can't make an APK. Revisit (xbuild or Gradle with GameActivity) when Bevy is upgraded.

name: samply
description: The profiler. No project uses it yet.

name: criterion
description: Benchmarks and regression reports. No project uses it yet.

name: trycmd and vhs
description: Transcript tests for CLIs, and terminal recordings for PRs that change CLI output. Chosen in decision 0001; rollout not started.

name: Cast
description: The old monorepo CLI, replaced by mise and removed. Don't restore it or its project templates.

name: GitHub (Actions, Dependabot, CodeQL)
description: Approved vendor. Hosts the repo and runs all CI, CD, nightly runs and maintenance workflows on standard runners, which are free on this public repo.
claude: Official GitHub MCP server, which has a read-only mode; Claude Code's own GitHub integration.

billing.note: The billing usage API shows any charge this month. No API shows a personal account's card or Actions budget, so Jim checks those.

name: Cloudflare Pages
description: Approved vendor. Hosts the static web apps, deployed with wrangler pages deploy (direct upload, no Pages builds). New projects are created only through free-tiers.sh.
claude: Cloudflare MCP servers (Claude connector directory) and the Cloudflare Claude Code plugin with Workers, Wrangler and D1 skills.

billing.note: One Cloudflare account: Billing Read shows its payment methods and subscriptions. Jim's yearly check is a backstop.

name: Cloudflare Workers
description: Approved vendor, Free plan only. Written in Rust with workers-rs: tofu_state is OpenTofu's http state backend (decision 0009), telemetry takes events into Analytics Engine with a rate-limit binding (decision 0001), and pane/cloudflare serves pane's Dioxus build as Workers static assets and runs Rust only for /api/* (standards/tasks/cloudflare-worker-assets.toml). Web Analytics is planned. Workers are created only through free-tiers.sh worker.
claude: Cloudflare MCP servers (Claude connector directory) and the Cloudflare Claude Code plugin with Workers, Wrangler and D1 skills.

billing.note: Same account as Pages. The check fails on Workers Paid.

name: Cloudflare D1
description: The hosted database (decision 0004, Jim 2026-11-26), used only when a deployed service must write data at runtime, until a need comes up that it can't meet. Part of an approved vendor, Free plan only. First used by tofu_state for OpenTofu state (decision 0009).
claude: Cloudflare MCP servers (Claude connector directory) and the Cloudflare Claude Code plugin with Workers, Wrangler and D1 skills.

billing.note: Same account as Pages. D1 Free has no billing.

name: Cloudflare R2
description: R2 bills past its free allowance once it is enabled, so don't enable it without a decision record.
claude: Cloudflare MCP servers (Claude connector directory) and the Cloudflare Claude Code plugin with Workers, Wrangler and D1 skills.

billing.note: Same account as Pages. The check fails if R2 paid is turned on.

name: Squarespace
description: Approved vendor. Jim's existing account; no automation or project in the repo uses it.

billing.note: No public API for account billing. Jim pays for several domains there (2026-11-27), which the settings check confirms are the only charges until the cost framework tracks them.

name: Auth0
description: Approved exception, free plan. Always use it for sign-in (CIAM). Tests use mocks, never real tokens.
claude: Official Auth0 MCP server.

billing.note: The Management API has no plan, subscription or payment endpoint.

name: PostHog
description: Approved exception, free tier, for one job: real-user session replay (and game events) on production sites, with all text input masked. First used in cookbook (2026-11-27), loaded only on the production host.
claude: PostHog MCP connector in the Claude directory.

billing.note: GET /api/billing/ with a billing:read key shows any subscription or charge. Adding a card is what starts a subscription.

name: RapidAPI (Zillow data)
description: Approved exception for homer only, and only on its free plan. It must never cost money: no paid plan and no scheduled runs.

billing.note: No consumer billing API, and polling the quota header on a schedule would break homer's free-plan rule.

name: Cloudflare Flagship
description: Cloudflare's feature flag service, in public beta with pricing after GA not announced, and no workers-rs binding. Decision 0018 builds a small flags Worker on D1 and a management app per project instead, and revisits Flagship at GA.
claude: Cloudflare plugin (flagship skill) and the Cloudflare MCP server.

name: OpenFeature
description: CNCF standard API for feature flags. Decision 0018 shapes the in-house flags crate after it so a later provider change stays in one crate.

name: flagd, Unleash and GrowthBook
description: Open-source feature flag servers considered in decision 0018. Each needs a long-running server and a database with no free host among approved vendors, or a new hosted vendor, so don't start work on them.

name: Neon
description: Hosted Postgres with per-PR branches and scale to zero. Decision 0004 chose D1 first; Neon is revisited only if a need comes up that D1 can't meet. Not an approved vendor.
claude: Neon MCP connector in the Claude directory.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: SurrealDB
description: Used only by luggage (on hold). Decision 0004 puts committed files, committed SQLite and then D1 first, so don't start new work on it.

name: SpacetimeDB
description: Named in the standards README for real-time stateful sync, but no project has tried it.

name: Supabase and Turso
description: Compared in decision 0004 and not chosen: Supabase pauses idle projects and has paid-only branching; Turso blocks every database once any one limit is hit and is being acquired.
claude: Supabase MCP connector in the Claude directory.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: Honeycomb, Sentry and Microsoft Clarity
description: Considered for observability and session replay in decision 0001 and dropped in favour of Cloudflare plus PostHog, to keep the vendor count down.
claude: Sentry MCP connector in the Claude directory.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: RentCast, ATTOM and HouseCanary
description: Property data alternatives to RapidAPI. RentCast's free plan bills overage with no hard cap; ATTOM and HouseCanary are paid only.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: Free tiers only
description: Every service runs on its free plan; when a limit is near, stop rather than pay. Anything automation creates on demand goes through the free-tiers guard.

name: Fewest vendors, cost first
description: Reach for GitHub, Cloudflare and Squarespace first. Any other vendor needs Jim's sign-off in a decision record, unless it is clearly cheaper.

name: Decision records in the repo
description: Plans, decisions and retros are Markdown committed next to what they are about, never chat or hosted docs.

name: One file per issue
description: Each TODO or FIX is one Markdown file with front matter in the docs/issues/ folder of the project it belongs to, instead of GitHub issues or shared ISSUES.md lists, so parallel PRs don't conflict; tasks only a person can do go in that project's docs/issues/human/ (decisions 0002 and 0006). The list is generated by mise run //:issues.

name: Agent Skills
description: Repeatable agent procedures as skills in .agents/skills, validated on every PR, so the repo runs without a local clone.
claude: Native to Claude Code: skills in .claude/skills load automatically.

name: Draft-first PRs with an agent merge rule
description: PRs open as drafts, go ready only when green, and any agent may squash-merge a mergeable, approved PR. PR triage drives every PR to closure.

name: Nightly CI and CD
description: Every project runs CI every night, and every deployable project redeploys the latest main that passed, so drift shows up within a day.

name: Preview deploys and recorded smoke UAT
description: A preview per PR and @smoke Playwright tests recorded against previews and production, linked from the PR. Accepted in decision 0001; rollout under way.

name: Files before databases
description: Keep data and results as committed Markdown, JSON, JSON Lines, CSV or TOML; when real queries are needed, commit a SQLite .sql dump read with rusqlite; a hosted database (D1) is the last resort (AGENTS.md, decision 0004).

name: Eval engine for product requirements
description: Proposed in decision 0003: requirements with stable IDs, evals tied to each, verdicts computed after CI, CD, chaos runs and observation, plus in-app feedback from Jim. Results stay in committed files.

name: Shared design tokens (design_system)
description: One TOML source of colour, type and spacing tokens for five themes (earthy, airy, professional, colorful, gamey) in light, dark and accessible modes, plus custom app themes such as bear_down's Bears theme, generated as CSS custom properties for web apps and Rust constants for Bevy games, with WCAG contrast checked in CI. In use by pane/web (professional theme) since 2026-11-26; the other apps follow the plan's adoption order.

name: Shell scripts
description: The standards say to script in Rust, not shell. The repo scripts in standards/scripts are the existing exception; don't add shell scripts to projects.

name: Claude Code
description: Our AI coding platform (Jim, 2026-11-26): agents work the projects' docs/issues/ backlogs, open and triage PRs, and run the scheduled reviews and digests. Its support shapes other choices: prefer technologies and vendors Claude knows well or that have a Claude plugin or MCP server we can enable read-only. The one paid service: budget $25 a month (Jim, 2026-11-26).
claude: It is Claude. Skills, plugins and MCP servers extend it.

billing.note: claude.ai subscription billing has no API.

name: OpenTofu
description: Accepted in decision 0007 (Jim, 2026-11-26) as the IaC engine: plans and applies the Terraform JSON the infra crate synthesizes, with built-in state encryption and no account. Moves to Trial when its phase 1 merges.
claude: OpenTofu MCP server (registry and resource docs) and HashiCorp's Terraform MCP server, read-only.

name: Infrastructure as code synthesized from Rust
description: Accepted in decision 0007 (Jim, 2026-11-26): Rust constructs write committed Terraform JSON (*.tf.json), PR CI plans it, and main applies the saved plan, so generation and apply are decoupled. Dashboard settings move into code; drift is checked weekly.

name: CDKTF and CDK Terrain
description: CDKTF was archived by HashiCorp on 2025-12-10; its community fork CDK Terrain supports TypeScript, Python and Go only. No Rust, and it needs Node (decision 0007).

name: Pulumi
description: No Rust SDK, and its state service is a new vendor. Compared in decision 0007 and not chosen.
claude: Pulumi MCP server.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: Crossplane
description: Needs an always-on Kubernetes cluster, which no approved vendor offers free. Compared in decision 0007 and not chosen.

name: Terraform CLI and HCP Terraform
description: Business Source License, no state encryption, and HCP Terraform is a new vendor with a 500-resource free tier. OpenTofu reads the same providers and JSON (decision 0007).
claude: HashiCorp Terraform MCP server.

billing.note: No account, so nothing can bill. Moving it to Trial or Adopt needs a billing check first (RAD-007).

name: terrars
description: Generates strongly typed Rust bindings from Terraform provider schemas and writes .tf.json. Accepted in decision 0007 (Jim, 2026-11-26) as the typed layer under the infra crate's constructs. The phase 1 spike passed (2026-11-26): only the resource types we use are generated, which build in seconds. We fix bugs we find upstream rather than work around them (Jim, 2026-11-26).
